subject: Weekly exec staff update — wins, risks & QBR prep (Aug 31)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: QBR-Deck-Review@redwood-partners.io
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly exec staff update — wins, risks & QBR prep (Aug 31)

Team —

Short update ahead of the Thursday QBR dry run. Please read and flag anything that needs lifting to the exec presentation. I kept this tight: wins, top risks, and asks / owners.

WINS
- Hosted: 15% unit-cost drop after caching changes rolled to prod (batching + prefix cache). Observability shows 3% latency improvement for 1k–2k token requests.
- Dedicated: first customer migration (Orbit Analytics) completed with zero data-leak incidents in the runbook test.
- Console: new token-level cost view landed in staging; UX feedback positive from CS.

RISKS / CONCERNS
- QBR narrative: we need a clearer explanation of the cost/levers tradeoff for customers who need <50ms P95. Ops ask: quantify the latency vs quantization trade for the top 3 model families. (Owner: Karthik)
- Contracts: Stratus Bank procurement still needs an SOC 2 gap confirmation; legal and security need to confirm wording by Wed EOD or we push the signature into next week. (Owner: Olga)
- Capacity: Dedicated pool autoscaler occasionally mis-evaluates GPU readiness under sustained 95th percentile; this shows up as short spikes in queueing. On-call is triaging; we should be ready with a rollback knife if spikes hit SLAs during QBR demo. (Owner: Marcus)

ASKS (short, actionable)
1) Karthik: provide 1 slide with concrete numbers — token-cost delta vs P95 latency across CPU, A100, and H100-like profiles. Needed by Wed 5pm. (attachment: QBR-OKR-scoringsheet.xlsx)
2) Olga: confirm SOC 2 statement wording and whether we can provide the customer redline. Target: Wed noon.
3) Vanessa: consolidate the action list and slide-owner mapping; run one last visual pass on deck before Thursday dry run.
4) Laura: open with a 90-second exec-readout frame for QBR (high-level outcomes & ask). Can you draft?

Attachments: 2026Q3_QBR_prelim_slide_deck_v1.pptx (pptx), QBR-OKR-scoringsheet.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — keep it short in replies so we can resolve owners quickly.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly exec staff update — wins, risks & QBR prep (Aug 31)

Thanks Marcus — good summary. A few quick notes:

- I can take the 90-second frame. Will draft 2 variants: one for enterprise (Stratus emphasis) and one for platform-wide audience. Sending first pass by Wed 11am.
- For the QBR narrative on cost/levers: can Karthik include a short sentence on expected user experience delta (e.g., quality drift estimate) when moving from FP16->4-bit quantization? Execs will want to hear tradeoffs in plain language.

On SOC 2 redline: Olga, if Security confirms we can provide a limited confirmation (no raw artifacts) that should unblock procurement for a signature. If not, we should consider a 2-week controlled access plan.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

On the numbers: I pulled the perf matrix this morning and started a one-slide draft. Key pointers:

- For P95 < 50ms: only A100/H100 configs realistically hit that for 1–2k token spans without compromising throughput; cost delta vs our baseline is ~2.3x on tokens.
- 4-bit quant: typical quality drift is measurable for code-heavy completions and long-context summarization; show with a single customer example (Orbit) rather than abstract metrics.

Deliverables:
- Slide: latency vs unit-cost (A100/H100/CPU) + one note line on quality drift with an Orbit example. Due Wed 5pm to Marcus.
- Short text blurb for Laura: plain-language two-liner on what customers trade when they pick ultra-low latency. Due Wed 11am.

Forwarding the current draft to QBR-Deck-Review for comments.

— Karthik
